## Why an Elastic IP matters for DNS

A reverse proxy that terminates TLS (see [Configure SSL](configure-ssl.qmd)) needs a hostname that reliably points at the instance. An [Elastic IP](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/elastic-ip-addresses-eip.html) is a static public address that stays with your AWS account. Allocate one before you create the DNS record. Without it, a stopped and restarted instance comes back with a new public address, and the record goes stale until someone repoints it.
